name: Wisconsin
overview: Wisconsin combines refundable homestead relief, a nonrefundable income-tax property/rent credit, veteran refunds and several separate property-bill credits.

programs.name: Homestead Credit
programs.ageRule: 18 or older; positive earned income, disability, or claimant/spouse age 62 or older also required.
programs.incomeDefinition: Broad taxable/nontaxable household income, loss/depreciation adjustments and $500 qualifying-dependent deduction.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-adjusted credit based on allowable assessed property taxes or rent constituting property taxes: 20% of rent when heat is included and 25% when heat is excluded.
programs.application: File Schedule H or H-EZ with tax bill/rent certificate; most 2025 claims due April 15, 2030.
eligibilityNotes: Public assistance and tax-exempt housing can affect allowance.
interactions: The claimant or spouse cannot claim Homestead credit if either claims the veterans/surviving-spouses property-tax credit or farmland preservation credit for the same taxable year.

The statute applies the credit exclusions to claims relating to the same taxable year. The 2025 Schedule H instructions instead refer to a veterans credit based on 2025 property taxes payable in 2026; those timing descriptions can identify different returns.
programs.programYear: 2025 household income, rent and assessed property taxes; tax-year-2025 claims generally begin filing in 2026.

programs.name: School Property Tax Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: $300 ordinarily, or $150 for married filing separately and married head-of-household filers, limited by income-tax liability.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-tax credit based on eligible property taxes or rent; owner and renter amounts share one cap. Rent constituting property taxes equals 20% of rent when heat is included and 25% when heat is excluded.
eligibilityNotes: Uses taxes paid in 2025, unlike Homestead's assessed-tax basis.
interactions: The claimant or spouse cannot claim School Property Tax Credit if either claims the veterans/surviving-spouses property-tax credit for the same taxable year.

The statute applies the credit exclusions to claims relating to the same taxable year. The 2025 Schedule H instructions instead refer to a veterans credit based on 2025 property taxes payable in 2026; those timing descriptions can identify different returns.
programs.programYear: 2025 income-tax return, using eligible property taxes and rent paid in 2025.

programs.name: Veterans and Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: WDVA-certified eligible veteran or unremarried surviving spouse.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible principal-dwelling taxes. DOR guidance limits land to one acre; disputed statutory acreage cases remain unresolved.
programs.formulaSummary: Refunds qualifying paid property taxes; excludes special assessments, interest, service charges and business-use taxes.
programs.application: Obtain WDVA certification and claim through income-tax return.
eligibilityNotes: An otherwise qualified renter may claim actual property taxes required by a written landlord agreement and paid directly to the municipality. Ordinary rent is not a percentage-based tax proxy.
DOR instructions specify one acre, while the statute cross-refers to a principal-dwelling definition without a numeric acreage limit. Disputed acreage claims remain unresolved.
interactions: The claimant or spouse cannot claim School Property Tax, Homestead or farmland preservation credits for the same taxable year when claiming this veterans credit.

The statute applies the credit exclusions to claims relating to the same taxable year. The 2025 Schedule H instructions instead refer to a veterans credit based on 2025 property taxes payable in 2026; those timing descriptions can identify different returns.
programs.programYear: 2025 income-tax return, using qualifying municipal property-tax payments made in 2025.

programs.name: Lottery and Gaming Credit
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested; household income is not used to calculate this bill credit.
programs.maximumBenefit: Applicable annual equalized school-tax rate × the smaller of the qualifying dwelling’s estimated fair market value and $27,000. The $27,000 figure is a value base for December 2025 bills, not a cash maximum.
programs.formulaSummary: Parcel bill reduction using the annual municipality/school-district rate and capped value base, subject to valid claim, parcel tax liability and installment rules.
programs.application: Apply to the county or eligible city treasurer. A missing 2025 bill credit may be claimed through the municipal treasurer by January 31, 2026, or by late DOR application through October 1, 2026.
eligibilityNotes: Wisconsin resident-owner principal dwelling on January 1, 2025; a documented buyer-after-January 1 exception can preserve a predecessor-qualified parcel’s credit.
A new dwelling must be completed and occupied on the relevant January 1. First Dollar eligibility alone does not establish Lottery eligibility.
Credit stays with a qualifying parcel on sale; multiple-property and separate-spouse cases require their specific facts.
interactions: May coexist with First Dollar and School Levy credits.
Bill reductions affect net general taxes actually paid; the veterans credit uses its separate qualified municipal-payment ledger and calendar year.
A tax payment already reduced by the credit does not receive another subtraction; a correction refund is not a second award.

programs.name: First Dollar Credit
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested; household income is not used to calculate this bill credit.
programs.maximumBenefit: Applicable annual equalized school-tax rate × the smaller of total qualifying parcel estimated fair market value and $9,000. The $9,000 figure is a value base for December 2025 bills, not a cash maximum.
programs.formulaSummary: Automatic credit for taxable real-estate parcels with a real-property improvement. The improvement establishes eligibility; total parcel value determines the capped base.
eligibilityNotes: Business, commercial, rental and nonprincipal improved real-estate parcels can qualify; one owner can receive credits on multiple parcels.
Personal-property improvements do not qualify. Manufactured homes qualify only when correctly classified as real property; monthly-permit-fee homes do not receive First Dollar.
interactions: May coexist with Lottery and School Levy credits.
Applied evenly across installments; Lottery applies to the first installment before First Dollar, subject to nonnegative tax liability.
No separate renter payment or income-tax-return credit.

programs.name: School Levy Tax Credit
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested; household income is not used to calculate this bill credit.
programs.formulaSummary: The state allocates School Levy funding using each municipality’s share of three-year average school levies. The parcel amount is allocated by assessed value within the municipality and is already reflected in net levy/tax figures.
programs.application: Applied through local property-tax billing, not income-tax return.
eligibilityNotes: Applies to every taxable real-property parcel, including vacant, rental and commercial property; no primary-residence requirement.
This is property-owner bill relief, not a direct renter payment.
interactions: May coexist with Lottery and First Dollar credits.
Net school levies and the bill’s net tax or rate already reflect this credit; the informational School Levy box does not provide an additional reduction.
The separate School Property income-tax credit and the veterans income-tax credit have different rules.
programs.programYear: 2025 assessment/property-tax bills issued in December 2025, normally payable in 2026. State May/July 2026 distributions finance the same bill credit.

sources.title: 2025 School Levy Tax Credit notice and 2026 distribution

researchNotes: Lottery/Gaming, First Dollar and School Levy credits normally already reduce net property-tax bills. A net tax payment excludes those credits.
School Property Tax Credit and School Levy Tax Credit follow different rules.
Veteran eligibility requires WDVA certification and the other statutory conditions. A disability-percentage input alone does not establish eligibility.

For the three bill credits, 2025 assessment and December billing generally precede 2026 collection. Local parameters, ownership history, installment limits and corrected bills remain necessary for a calculation; the listed value caps are not cash awards.
